metaDescription: NSIC Rc 732 is an inbred rice for rainfed lowland: about 110 days and 4.8 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 732 is an inbred rice variety for rainfed lowland, known locally as Sahod Ulan 37. The NSIC approved it in 2023. PhilRice bred it. It matures in about 110 days and averages 4.8 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 7 tonnes in trials.

**Cooked rice:** high amylose, so firm and fluffy.

blocks.caption: Key facts of NSIC Rc 732 (t/ha means tonnes per hectare)

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 732 yield?

On average it gives 4.8 tonnes per hectare. That is about 96 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits above the average of the 25 rainfed lowland inbreds on the list, which is 3.4 tonnes. But the top yield, 7 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 110 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

Amylose decides how rice cooks. With high amylose, expect rice that is firm and dry, and it hardens as it cools. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits rainfed lowland that depends on the rains. So wait until the rains settle before you sow the seedbed, then transplant into the puddled field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 732?
items.a: It is known as Sahod Ulan 37. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 732 take to harvest?
items.a: About 110 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 732?
items.a: It averages 4.8 tonnes per hectare, about 96 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 7 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
It has high amylose, 23.2 percent. So it cooks firm and fluffy, and hardens as it cools.
